clue.text: Old coat of rags concealing ample bust for models

indicators.note: a coat is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept
something bust is broken, so its letters are smashed and put back together differently
to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: ex- means former or old
the first and last letters of the word
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tatty old coat stretched over a large bust, worn by fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ample bust' reads as a body part, but 'bust' is the signal to break up the word; 'Old' and the coat letters join to make the outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplars are examples worth copying, the sense of models as patterns to imitate.

clue.text: Fetching dresses make an impression

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, so the outer word wraps around the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: An attractive outfit catches the eye and makes a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching dresses' looks like attractive clothes, but 'dresses' is a verb: fETCHing wears the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut lines into a hard surface, literally leaving a mark or indentation.

clue.text: As it happens, revolutionary is wrong

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a broadcast shown as it happens is live

explanation.surface: A remark that, as things turn out, being a revolutionary is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' feels like a throwaway phrase, but it defines live, as in a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil as a noun means wickedness or wrongdoing, matching wrong used as a noun for misdeed.

clue.text: Mug knocked over with hot drink left for Easter

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: a mug is a gullible fool, as is a sap
cha is a British slang word for tea
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A mug of hot chocolate knocked over and left behind at Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup to go with the drink, but it means a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Paschal is the adjective relating to Easter or Passover, from the Latin for the festival.

clue.text: Model answer about writer

blocks.note: to model for an artist is to pose
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A sample answer discussing an author, as in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model answer' reads as an exemplary reply; split it into two pieces and turn them round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author credited with the famous collection of animal fables.

clue.text: Identified coins banks provided with old penny

indicators.note: banks line both sides of a river, so one piece flanks the other

blocks.note: specie is money in the form of coins
'provided' means on condition that, like if
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone recognised which coins banks handed over along with an old penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the institutions dealing in coins, but it is a verb: the coin word lines both sides of a condition word.
explanation.definitionFit: To specify something is to name or state it precisely, so specified means named or picked out.

clue.text: Lavish person boozing after opening of Pinot

indicators.note: the opening of anything is its start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the wine name
a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish' could describe the drinker in the surface, but it is the definition; 'after' places the drinker behind the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush means luxurious and expensively furnished, close in sense to lavish or opulent.

clue.text: Old city‘s ceremony — bet it is occasionally ignored

blocks.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
the second, fourth and sixth letters, with the rest dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters come from the even positions of the three words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii is the Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Love may be so fully embraced by a French revolutionary

blocks.note: quite can mean completely
un is the French for a
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' after 2-down suggests reversal again, but here it is RED, wrapped round the word for fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequited love is a passion not returned by its object, a familiar idiom of romantic poetry.

clue.text: Clue antelope crosses river in remote area

blocks.note: a hint is a clue
an eland is a large African antelope
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clue' sounds like a crossword-about-crosswords word, but it simply gives HINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinterland is the remote back country lying far behind a coast or major town.

clue.text: Fries cold joints

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hips are joints of the body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fries' looks like a verb about cooking joints of meat, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is the British word for thin fried potato strips, which Americans call french fries.

clue.text: It’s used when pressing matter is resolved, saving time working

indicators.note: to resolve can mean to break down into parts, so the letters are reformed
saving can mean except, so one letter is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, here removed
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Something deployed once an urgent issue is settled, saving time at work.

explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is the household appliance that smooths clothes with heat and vapour while ironing them.

clue.text: Like comic actor‘s crack in sequel that’s shot

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to chap is to crack, as skin does in the cold
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the silent film comedian, and the -esque suffix means in the style of him.

clue.text: Oats for one head of hotel, wanting European supply

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so one letter goes missing
supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European, here removed

explanation.surface: A hotel manager short of European supplies of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of hotel' wants to give H, but all three words are fodder, and 'supply' is not a noun but means flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a classic example of wholesome, natural fare sold as nourishing diet produce.

clue.text: Makes very dear papa paella, say, during parts of match

clue.text: Cover staff back after a lot of resentment

going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: envy loses its final letter
a staff is a long pole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees covering a shift, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or surround something completely, so it covers it.

clue.text: Standard places to eat last of Victoria sponges

indicators.note: the last of anything is its end, so only the final letter is kept
eating takes something inside, so the outer pieces swallow a letter

blocks.note: par is the normal or standard level
sites are places
the final letter of the name

clue.text: Letter from India, one put in language from the east

putting one thing in another places it inside

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Latin is a language
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first character of a name, so it is a single alphabetic character.

clue.text: Drink from well in East London

blocks.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

clue.text: More corpulent setter breaks into food store

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
a larder is a pantry

explanation.definitionFit: Lardy is informal for fat, so its comparative describes someone fatter or more portly.

clue.text: Somewhat antipathetic, in essence displaying this?

definitions.text: Somewhat antipathetic, in essence displaying this?

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and through the next two

explanation.surface: Someone a little hostile at heart shows this quality.

explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is a chilly, unfriendly manner, which is what an antipathetic person shows towards others.

clue.text: Duff intel going around over offence

the final letter of the word

clue.text: Form of address once for large figure

clue.text: Old French bread accompanying power lunch?
